Ngắm con đường dự kiến mang tên Nguyễn Bá Thanh ở Đà Nẵng
Lãnh đạo UBND TP Đà Nẵng đã thống nhất đề xuất tuyến ĐT605, đoạn kéo dài từ quốc lộ 1 đến giáp cầu Cẩm Lý, mang tên cố Bí thư Thành ủy Đà Nẵng Nguyễn Bá Thanh.
Theo Sở Văn hóa, Thể thao và Du lịch Đà Nẵng, qua rà soát, hiện thành phố chưa có tuyến đường nào mang tên cố Bí thư Thành ủyNguyễn Bá Thanh.
Đà Nẵng khảo sát tuyến đường dự kiến đặt tên Phan Văn Khải, Nguyễn Bá Thanh
Để chủ động trong công tác đặt, đổi tên đường và công trình công cộng, Sở Văn hóa, Thể thao và Du lịch đề xuất cố Bí thưThành ủy Đà NẵngNguyễn Bá Thanh vào trong quỹ tên đường của thành phố.

Việc lựa chọn một tuyến đường có quy mô lớn, vị trí phù hợp để đặt tên nhằm thể hiện sự tri ân, tôn vinh những đóng góp to lớn của các bậc tiền nhân đối với sự nghiệp cách mạng và phát triển quê hương, đất nước.
Đồng thời, việc đặt tên đường bảo đảm đáp ứng yêu cầu quản lý đô thị và nguyện vọng của nhân dân thành phố.
Đoạn đường đi qua khu vực trung tâm hành chính xã Hòa Tiến (cũ) - Ảnh: ĐOÀN CƯỜNG
Đoạn từ nút giao quốc lộ 1 rẽ vào ĐT605 - Ảnh: ĐOÀN CƯỜNG
Về phương án đề xuất đặt tên đường cố Bí thư Thành ủy Đà Nẵng Nguyễn Bá Thanh:
Trên cơ sở khảo sát thực tế và các đợt đề xuất trước đây của UBND xã Hòa Tiến, Sở Văn hóa, Thể thao và Du lịch đã chọn tuyến đường ĐT605.
Đây là tuyến đường thuộc địa phận xã Hòa Tiến, quê hương của ông.
Trên tuyến này có đường đặt tên Anh hùng Lực lượng vũ trang nhân dân Nguyễn Bá Tùng là cha ruột của cố Bí thư Thành ủy Đà Nẵng Nguyễn Bá Thanh.
Từ đường ĐT605 vào mộ ông Nguyễn Bá Thanh khá gần - Ảnh: ĐOÀN CƯỜNG
Người dân đến thắp hương cho ông Nguyễn Bá Thanh chiều 4-11 - Ảnh: ĐOÀN CƯỜNG

Tại cuộc họp chiều 4-11,UBND TP Đà Nẵngđã "chốt" phương án chọn tuyến đường ĐT605, đoạn từ quốc lộ 1 đến cầu Cẩm Lý (đoạn giáp ranh giữa phường Điện Bàn Bắc và phường Điện Bàn Tây) để đề xuất đặt tên ông Nguyễn Bá Thanh.
Theo ghi nhận, tuyến ĐT605 có mặt cắt rộng 26m, gồm vỉa hè mỗi bên 5m, có 4 làn xe (mỗi bên 2 làn).
Mặt đường đã được thảm nhựa, hai bên có cây xanh.
Khu vực trung tâm của xã Hòa Tiến (cũ) - Ảnh: ĐOÀN CƯỜNG
Đoạn qua khu vực trung tâm hành chính xã Hòa Tiến (cũ) nhà cửa khang trang, vỉa hè khá đẹp, cảnh quan xanh mát.
Tại đoạn nút ĐT605 với quốc lộ 1, tuyến đường cũng kết nối với khu vực dự kiến đặt tên cố Thủ tướngPhan Văn Khảicho đoạn quốc lộ 1 từ cầu Đỏ đến giáp đường Hùng Vương, phường Điện Bàn Bắc.
Đoạn quốc lộ 1 dự kiến đặt tên cố Thủ tướng Phan Văn Khải.
Đoạn này sẽ đi qua nút giao với đường ĐT605 - dự kiến đặt tên ông Nguyễn Bá Thanh - Ảnh: ĐOÀN CƯỜNG
Từ nút giao này đến khu mộ ông Nguyễn Bá Thanh chỉ khoảng 3km.
Tuyến ĐT605 cũng giao với đường Nguyễn Bá Tùng (cha ruột của cố Bí thư Thành ủy Đà Nẵng Nguyễn Bá Thanh).
Ông Nguyễn Bá Thanh (1953 - 2015) từng giữ chức vụ Chủ tịch UBND TP Đà Nẵng, Bí thư Thành ủy Đà Nẵng, Trưởng Ban Nội chính Trung ương.
Trong suốt thời gian làm lãnh đạo thành phố Đà Nẵng, ông Thanh đã góp phần làm thay đổi diện mạo đô thị thành phố này.
Cử tri đề nghị sớm xem xét, đặt tên đường Nguyễn Bá Thanh, sở trả lời gì?
Sở Văn hóa, Thể thao và Du lịch Đà Nẵng vừa trả lời kiến nghị của cử tri liên quan việc đặt tên đường mang tên ông Nguyễn Bá Thanh.

White House panel delays hearing on Fed's Lisa Cook to Dec. 14Skip Navigation
MarketsBusinessInvestingTechPolitics & PolicyVideoWatchlistInvesting ClubPROLivestreamMenu
A special committee appointed by President Donald Trump has rescheduled a hearing for Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook for Dec. 14, a White House official said.
Trump in early October established a "committee of inquiry" to investigate allegations that Cook made false statements related to "one or more mortgage instruments."
The Supreme Court in June had barred Trump from firing Cook, for now, because he failed to give due process in trying to summarily terminate her in Aug. 2025.
Federal Reserve Board Governor Lisa Cook participates in a board meeting at the Federal Reserve on March 19, 2026 in Washington, DC.Kevin Dietsch | Getty Images
A White Housecommittee of inquirypostponed from Thursday to Dec. 14 a hearing withFederal ReserveGovernorLisa Cookfor an investigation of whether allegations of false statements in mortgage applications warrant her firing by PresidentDonald Trump, a White House official said Wednesday evening.
But it was unclear if Cook, whom Trump unsuccessfullytried to firein August 2025, would agree to attend.
The official said the postponement came at the request of Cook.
Her lawyer Abbe Lowell last month said questions about the committee's fairness and objectivity would have to be addressed before the hearing could occur.
Lowell also said the hearing could not take place until December, at the earliest, because she "will be executing her official duties as Governor at financial and monetary policy meetings in Europe."

The New York Timesfirst reported the hearing's rescheduling.
Trump in early October established the committee to investigate allegations that Cook made false statements related to "one or more mortgage instruments."
"The Committee shall investigate the allegations against Governor Cook and report to me whether there is 'cause' for Governor Cook's removal within the meaning of" a federal law that was cited in a Supreme Court ruling in June that temporarily blocked her firing.
The committee is comprised of Kevin Hassett, assistant to the president for economic policy, Andrea Lucas, the chair of the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission, and Office of Government Ethics Director Keith Sonderling.
In a lawsuit challenging her firing, she argued that Trump's claim about the mortgage statements is pretextual, and that his real reason for trying to oust her is her refusal to agree to his demands that she vote for lower interest rates.
Trump created the panel more than three months after the Supreme Court ruled that the president, for now, could not fire Cook from the central bank's board.
The ruling kept in place a lower court's order preventing Cook from being terminated while the suit challenging her dismissal proceeds.
The decision did not determine whether Trump ultimately has the power to fire a Fed board member. But it said she could remain on the board as her suit was pending because she was not given due process to challenge her firing.
The committee of inquiry Trump set up may be designed to show the Supreme Court that Cook has now received due process.

Knicks players reportedly say no to White House visit and James Dolan isn't happy about it
TheKnicksstopped their winless drought with a 111-97 win over thePistonson Tuesday, benefitting from a 27-point, 20-rebound display by Karl-Anthony Towns. Despite this, the 1-3 team remains a topic of conversation for all the wrong reasons in the Big Apple.
A slight championship hangover could be forgiven following New York's triumph in the Finals. A 1-3 record, coupled with speculation over Towns and Josh Hart's future? Well, that's a little harder to grapple with.
New York hasn't been the picture of consistency it proved itself to be during last year's playoffs. One man has faced much of the blame for that deviation — James Dolan.
With that, here are the latest rumors on Dolan and his relationship with the team, as provided by ESPN's Stephen A. Smith on Wednesday morning.

Knicks players reportedly say no to White House visit
Smith authored up an epic diatribe against Dolan, a man he dubbed the "walking embodiment of petulance."
Smith claimed that Dolan might be embroiled in a feud with the Knicks players amid rumors that they will reject a White House invitation.
"This is what I've been hearing and I'm going to say it. I don't know how much truth there is to it because I haven't heard from the players directly," Smith said. "One of the things that people have been talking about around New York City...is that the climate has been a little bit different, people have been a little bit stressed. The owner James Dolan has an attitude with players because they don't want to go to the White House."
"The owner James Dolan has an attitude with players because they don't want to go to the White House" – Stephen A. Smith on what he's hearing about the New York Knicks https://t.co/ufJtKvqPjK
— Awful Announcing (@awfulannouncing)October 28, 2026
Smith admitted that he didn't know whether the allegations were true. In September, head coach Mike Brown told reporters that the team hadn't yet decided whether it would accept Trump's invitation.
"No, it's still something that our guys, or the organization, is internally discussing and, you know, whatever we decide to do, we'll all do together," Brown said, perESPN.
Smith told his First Take colleagues that while he isn't sure whether the report is true, he wouldn't be surprised if it was. He also questioned Dolan's aptitude as an owner.
"He's the kind of guy that will sit up back and be like 'This ring is going to last another 25 years,'" Smith said. "As opposed to a great owner like Joe Lacob or, God bless his wonderful soul, the late, great George Steinbrenner. Wasn't satisfied with one [championship], wanted more.
"This guy Dolan, I don't trust him. I don't trust him one bit. I think that complacency is something he could definitely be a part of. He is petty enough to have an attitude because he's tight with Trump and wants to go to the White House and some of the players, if not most of them, might not want to go."
Trump and Dolan are certainly close. The Knicks owner hosted his wedding at Trump's Mar-a-Lago residence in 2002. He has returned the favor throughout Trump's political career, helping bankroll his campaigns. Dolan called him a friend in a 2018 interview withESPN. The two made the closeness of their relationship all the more evident when Dolan invited Trump to Madison Square Garden as a guest to watch the Knicks andSpurs' Game 3 matchup in the NBA Finals.
All of that is to say, it's not impossible to believe that Dolan — a renowned enjoyer of surveillance tech who came under fire after a Wired investigation found that Dolan employs facial recognition to track and profile arena attendees, namely a trans woman who was targeted solely due to her gender identity, per a former security staffer — would want to impose his personal and political leanings on those who he writes his paychecks for.
Nevertheless, until we get more reporting, Smith's insights will prove little more than rumors that swirl around New York for the upcoming season.

In his free time, he enjoys skateboarding (poorly), listening to the likes of Stevie Wonder, Marvin Gaye and D’Angelo, and penning short journal entries.

Champions League Power Rankings: PSG hold top spot as Como surge under Cesc Fabregas
PSG lead the pack through four matchdays as Como surge behind a nine-goal explosion and Liverpool stumble during a chaotic week
ByChuck BoothNov 4, 2026at 7:49 pm ET•1 min readGetty Images
Four matchdays are behind us, and everyone is still chasingParisSaint-Germain. PSG haven't let injuries to key players like Ousmane Dembele and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia stop them from hanging crooked numbers on teams around the world, but even they couldn't match Como, who put nine goals past Lens. Under Cesc Fabregas, Como have become an absolute unit and are rolling up the power rankings because of that. They've yet to enter the PSG,Arsenal,Barcelona, andReal Madridtier of contenders, but as Nico Paz improves, Como aren't far off.
There was plenty of carnage in the middle, withLiverpool,Real Betis, andRomaall dropping points. But that's also the beauty of the league phase: no one is out of a match, and it's impossible to predict everything correctly. No one hadManchester Unitedending their nine-match winless run against Roma, but that's also what makes soccer great. For 90 minutes, it seemed likeAEK Athenswere going to get a point off Real Madrid, but that also wasn't able to hold up, while City also were pushed to the brink byRB Leipzig. These are the things that make Champions League soccer so great, but they also mean that it's another week with plenty of shifts in the power rankings, so let's get to those:
Biggest Movers6Galatasaray7VillarrealRkTeamsChgRcrd1PSGIt doesn't matter who is in Luis Enrique's lineup; PSG just go out and win soccer matches, and they did just that on an away trip to Spain. With a four-goal lead before the 20-minute mark, it's impossible to view anyone other than PSG as the favorites to win this competition, even as Ousmane Dembele and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia miss time due to injuries.--4-02Real MadridThey can't keep getting away with this. Trailing in the 75th minute, Real Madrid scored twice to join PSG as the only teams with a perfect record through four UCL matches. Madrid are flawed, but we know flawed Real Madrid teams thrive in European play.--4-03BarcelonaBarcelona managed their emotions while earning a shutout victory over Aston Villa. Hansi Flick's team are deep, but he'll hope that depth isn't tested too much more now that Rodri will miss some time.--3-14ArsenalAnother match where Arsenal did exactly what was expected of them. After going ahead 2-0 in the first half and holding off Slavia Prague in the second, results like this can't be taken for granted, as other sides have struggled to make it look this easy. You just can't ease off late and allow goals that could come back to bite you.--8-15Manchester CityGianluigi Donnarumma is making things harder than they need to be for City, but they still have a heat-seeking missile in Erling Haaland to clean up any issues. There's plenty of room for improvement, but a win is a win.17-26BayernFor another side short on bodies due to injuries, going to Atletico Madrid and securing a win was a gritty result. Harry Kane may not have scored, but he showcased his Ballon d'Or credentials. Defenses can't forget about him, or they'll be picking the ball out of the net, even if it's a goal the English forward created rather than scored.12-07Sporting CPAfter suffering a setback on matchday three, Sporting weathered the storm to get right back to where they expect to be. This isn't a team that will truly trouble the contenders, but Sporting are right in that next tier of squads who can make a few things happen, especially if they keep scoring when Luis Suarez isn't involved.23-18ComoSheesh, save some goals for everyone else! This team is electric, and it'll be fascinating to see what they can accomplish under Cesc Fabregas with Nico Paz coming into his own. Como became the first team to score nine goals away from home in the post-European Cup era, and that attack is one to be feared.47-19LiverpoolLiverpool suffered their first league-phase loss in some fashion, allowing two goals in only six minutes and failing to come back. They're still sitting fine in the table, but Andoni Iraola's men have struggled to find any consistency so far this season.44-210Borussia DortmundSerhou Guirassy going off with an injury will be a cause for concern, but Dortmund got production from all over the pitch to see off a strong Real Betis side. The growth Fabio Silva has shown has been impressive, and it could bode very well moving forward.33-111Real BetisBetis didn't even reach 1.0 xG, as chances were hard to come by against Dortmund. They've been one of the surprises of the competition, but this match showed how wide the gap still is.33-112Aston VillaPerfect no more, Aston Villa ran into a buzzsaw. These are the kinds of games you chalk up to experience when you're Villa, but this is also when the gap between Europe's haves and have-nots shows.23-113Atletico MadridAtletico are still trying to show they can hang with the true contenders, and registering only three shots on target against Bayern Munich isn't the way to do that. Falling like a rock in the league phase to the point where they're now behind LASK is a bad look.21-214RomaRoma are allergic to two-goal leads, and everything unraveled at Old Trafford. After seeing this happen against both Manchester United and Real Madrid, something has to change.--1-215InterAfter losing the Milan derby, Inter needed a bit of good fortune, and they got just that in their win over Feyenoord. Inter are still worse off than last season's Scudetto-winning team, but that doesn't mean they can be ignored in the UCL.12-216StuttgartWith a chance to truly establish themselves as a top-eight side, Stuttgart struggled away from home. After a good campaign so far, they'll hope this is just a blip rather than the start of a new trend.12-117Club BruggeThrough Nicolo Tresoldi, all things are possible, as the young German found the net yet again to lift this dark-horse side higher in the table. Como's players take in the acclaim after the 9-1 rout at Lens.Photograph: Jean-François Badias/APView image in fullscreenComo's players take in the acclaim after the 9-1 rout at Lens.Photograph: Jean-François Badias/AP
Champions League: Como clobber Lens 9-1 after Real Madrid roar back to deny AEK Athens
Valverde hits late winner as Madrid win 3-2 in Athens
Napoli thrashed by Porto, Club Brugge win at PSV
Anastasios Douvikas led the rout with a hat-trick asComocruised to a 9-1 victory atLens, equalling the record for the most goals scored in a singleChampions Leaguegame.
Only two teams had previously won a game by a margin of eight goals since the launch of the modern Champions League in 1992. Liverpool thumped Besiktas 8-0 in the group stage in 2007 andReal Madridwon by the same scoreline against Malmo in 2015.
Muriqi caps Fenerbahce comeback to make Liverpool pay for defensive lapsesRead more
Como are just the second team to score nine times in a game in the competition, after Bayern Munich beat Dinamo Zagreb 9-2 in the league phase in 2024.
Cesc Fàbregas’s side made it three wins from four in their maiden campaign in the competition with a spellbinding display.
Nico Paz continued his fine form with a goal and two assists, while Lucas Da Cunha, Marc-Oliver Kempf, Mattia Liberali, Martin Baturina and Matteo Papaccioli also scored for the Serie A side, who had already beaten both RB Leipzig and Manchester United 4-1 at home in this campaign.
The last club to score nine away from home in the European Cup was Feyenoord against Olympiakos in 1971.
Federico Valverde lashed home a stunning effort from distance to snatchReal Madrida late 3-2 victory atAEK Athenson Wednesday and preserve their 100% start in the group phase.
View image in fullscreenReal Madrid players pile on top of Federico Valverde after the midfielder’s 90th-minute winner in Athens.Photograph: Petros Giannakouris/AP
José Mourinho’s side, who started with Vinícius Júnior on the left flank after he missed the team’s previous two La Liga matches through suspension, twice came from behind against the Greek champions before Valverde claimed all three points for his side.
Aboubakary Koïta sent AEK ahead after 12 minutes before Jude Bellingham equalised with a sublime flick for the record 15-time winners.
Stavros Pilios sent the Greek champions ahead with 15 minutes to go but Kylian Mbappé swiftly pulled Madrid level once again, setting the stage for Valverde’s late winner.
Madrid have now won seven successive games across all competitions.
Scott McTominay found the net butNapoliendured a 4-1 defeat byPorto, who had lost their first three games in the competition, whileClub Bruggeare up to ninth after a 2-1 win atPSV.
Konstantinos Karetsas struck a 72nd-minute winner asBorussia DortmundbeatReal Betis2-1, while Erik Botheim helped himself to two goals asVikingsecured their first triumph with a 4-1 win against 10-manSabah.

PSG lead the pack through four matchdays as Como surge behind a nine-goal explosion and Liverpool stumble during a chaotic week
ByChuck BoothNov 4, 2026at 7:49 pm ET•1 min readGetty Images
Four matchdays are behind us, and everyone is still chasingParisSaint-Germain.

PSG haven't let injuries to key players like Ousmane Dembele and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia stop them from hanging crooked numbers on teams around the world, but even they couldn't match Como, who put nine goals past Lens.
Under Cesc Fabregas, Como have become an absolute unit and are rolling up the power rankings because of that.
They've yet to enter the PSG,Arsenal,Barcelona, andReal Madridtier of contenders, but as Nico Paz improves, Como aren't far off.
There was plenty of carnage in the middle, withLiverpool,Real Betis, andRomaall dropping points.
But that's also the beauty of the league phase: no one is out of a match, and it's impossible to predict everything correctly.
No one hadManchester Unitedending their nine-match winless run against Roma, but that's also what makes soccer great.
For 90 minutes, it seemed likeAEK Athenswere going to get a point off Real Madrid, but that also wasn't able to hold up, while City also were pushed to the brink byRB Leipzig.
These are the things that make Champions League soccer so great, but they also mean that it's another week with plenty of shifts in the power rankings, so let's get to those:
Biggest Movers6Galatasaray7VillarrealRkTeamsChgRcrd1PSGIt doesn't matter who is in Luis Enrique's lineup; PSG just go out and win soccer matches, and they did just that on an away trip to Spain.

With a four-goal lead before the 20-minute mark, it's impossible to view anyone other than PSG as the favorites to win this competition, even as Ousmane Dembele and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia miss time due to injuries.--4-02Real MadridThey can't keep getting away with this.
Trailing in the 75th minute, Real Madrid scored twice to join PSG as the only teams with a perfect record through four UCL matches.
Madrid are flawed, but we know flawed Real Madrid teams thrive in European play.--4-03BarcelonaBarcelona managed their emotions while earning a shutout victory over Aston Villa.
Hansi Flick's team are deep, but he'll hope that depth isn't tested too much more now that Rodri will miss some time.--3-14ArsenalAnother match where Arsenal did exactly what was expected of them.
After going ahead 2-0 in the first half and holding off Slavia Prague in the second, results like this can't be taken for granted, as other sides have struggled to make it look this easy.

You just can't ease off late and allow goals that could come back to bite you.--8-15Manchester CityGianluigi Donnarumma is making things harder than they need to be for City, but they still have a heat-seeking missile in Erling Haaland to clean up any issues.
There's plenty of room for improvement, but a win is a win.17-26BayernFor another side short on bodies due to injuries, going to Atletico Madrid and securing a win was a gritty result.
Harry Kane may not have scored, but he showcased his Ballon d'Or credentials.

Defenses can't forget about him, or they'll be picking the ball out of the net, even if it's a goal the English forward created rather than scored.12-07Sporting CPAfter suffering a setback on matchday three, Sporting weathered the storm to get right back to where they expect to be.

This isn't a team that will truly trouble the contenders, but Sporting are right in that next tier of squads who can make a few things happen, especially if they keep scoring when Luis Suarez isn't involved.23-18ComoSheesh, save some goals for everyone else!
This team is electric, and it'll be fascinating to see what they can accomplish under Cesc Fabregas with Nico Paz coming into his own.

Como became the first team to score nine goals away from home in the post-European Cup era, and that attack is one to be feared.47-19LiverpoolLiverpool suffered their first league-phase loss in some fashion, allowing two goals in only six minutes and failing to come back.

They're still sitting fine in the table, but Andoni Iraola's men have struggled to find any consistency so far this season.44-210Borussia DortmundSerhou Guirassy going off with an injury will be a cause for concern, but Dortmund got production from all over the pitch to see off a strong Real Betis side.
The growth Fabio Silva has shown has been impressive, and it could bode very well moving forward.33-111Real BetisBetis didn't even reach 1.0 xG, as chances were hard to come by against Dortmund.
They've been one of the surprises of the competition, but this match showed how wide the gap still is.33-112Aston VillaPerfect no more, Aston Villa ran into a buzzsaw.

These are the kinds of games you chalk up to experience when you're Villa, but this is also when the gap between Europe's haves and have-nots shows.23-113Atletico MadridAtletico are still trying to show they can hang with the true contenders, and registering only three shots on target against Bayern Munich isn't the way to do that.
Falling like a rock in the league phase to the point where they're now behind LASK is a bad look.21-214RomaRoma are allergic to two-goal leads, and everything unraveled at Old Trafford.

After seeing this happen against both Manchester United and Real Madrid, something has to change.--1-215InterAfter losing the Milan derby, Inter needed a bit of good fortune, and they got just that in their win over Feyenoord.

Inter are still worse off than last season's Scudetto-winning team, but that doesn't mean they can be ignored in the UCL.12-216StuttgartWith a chance to truly establish themselves as a top-eight side, Stuttgart struggled away from home.

After a good campaign so far, they'll hope this is just a blip rather than the start of a new trend.12-117Club BruggeThrough Nicolo Tresoldi, all things are possible, as the young German found the net yet again to lift this dark-horse side higher in the table.
They're playing with confidence, and it could very well pay off.--3-118GalatasarayAleksey Batrakov's UCL form of four goa

Meta’s Prometheus AI datacenter campus and supercluster project in New Albany, Ohio.Photograph: Jon Cherry/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenMeta’s Prometheus AI datacenter campus and supercluster project in New Albany, Ohio.Photograph: Jon Cherry/Getty Images
Datacenters were on the ballot. US voters rejected them
Voters approved nearly every datacenter moratorium that was on the ballot, dozens in total in Tuesday’s elections
Track live results from all 50 states
Send us your questions about the US midterms results and Democrats’ ‘blue wave’
There were three big losers in Tuesday’s midterm elections in the US: Donald Trump, Elon Musk and datacenters.
Datacenters, the facilities full of semiconductor chips that power artificial intelligence and a host of other online products, were on the ballot in elections in at least 40 jurisdictions across 10 states. Voters responded with a strong rebuke of the giant buildings, which have has become a symbol of the tech industry and AI.
In Ohio alone, at least 14 municipalities passed bans or restrictions on datacenter development, including in Sunbury, whereAmazonhas proposed a $2m datacenter project. In Maine, eight municipalities passed temporary datacenter moratoriums. In Emporio, Kansas, where a 1,000-acre gigawatt-scale datacenter was recently proposed, a ban on high-impact datacenters was approved by voters.
Voters approved nearly every datacenter moratorium that was on the ballot, dozens in total, with one notable exception: Hardwood, North Dakota. The small city of a population of less than 1,000 people voted down a bill that would imposerestrictions on datacenter development.
Where datacenters were not explicitly on the ballot, officials who have pushed back against their development were elected. InTexas, Democrat Gina Hinojosa, who secured a historical victory as governor on Tuesday night over her Republican opponent, has promised to impose moratoriums on their construction. She has pledged to implement greater restrictions on and community input into whether datacenters can be built. Towards the end of his tenure, Greg Abbott, her Republican opponent, had also tried to capitalize on anti-datacenter sentiment, demanding an end to electricity subsidies for them. He reversed his previous stance that had welcomed datacenters to the state.
Keisha Lance Bottoms, who became governor of Georgia, and Amy Acton, the newly elected governor ofOhio, have also pledged to implement moratoria on the construction of large datacenters.
Anti-datacenter sentiment has grown in the last few months has become a bipartisan issue. In May, Florida governor Ron DeSantis signed a bill imposing strict regulations on large-scale datacenters. Still, last night’s election solidified the overwhelming opposition to these centers of compute that have come to serve as a stand-in for the ultra wealthy and resource extraction by the AI industry.
“Data centers in space looking pretty appealing right now,” Elon Musk, who poured over $400m into supporting conservative candidates, posted on X.
Analyst Dan Ives said the results of the midterms are a clear sign that the pace of datacenter buildout will start to slow down.
“There is no way to sugarcoat that Democrats taking control especially over the Senate will create some major hurdles for AI and tech legislation in the Beltway over the next two years,” Ives said. Ives said he was particularly worried about Hinojosa who is a “known anti-datacenter politician”.
“The biggest worry of the night for tech investors and the AI trade was around the state of Texas where 25%-30% of data center gigawatts and capacity will come from,” he said.

Voters rebuff data centers in every ballot measure except oneSkip Navigation
MarketsBusinessInvestingTechPolitics & PolicyVideoWatchlistInvesting ClubPROLivestreamMenu
41 data center-related ballot measures were up for a vote in the 2026 midterm elections in 10 states.
Voters backed restrictions or rejected pro-development measures in nearly every contest with results available Wednesday, with Harwood, North Dakota, the exception.
Anti-data-center messaging also featured in major Democratic wins in Ohio and Texas, increasing political risk for the AI infrastructure buildout.

Theartificial intelligencedata centerboom hit a roadblock onelection night, further complicating the tech industry's historic expansion plans.
There were 41 local ballot measures in 10 states up for a vote on Tuesday that would place restrictions on the construction of data centers in different ways, according toBallotpedia.
Voters sided against data centers in each measure except one in Harwood, North Dakota, according to an analysis by Ballotpedia and additional results gathered by CNBC on Wednesday. The lone exception was Harwood, North Dakota, where voters rejected an added review of industrial projects, including data centers.
Ohio alone accounted for more than half of the measures, with 21 on the ballot. The issue also played out at the top of the ticket, where Democrat Sherrod Brown ousted Republican Sen. Jon Husted after casting the incumbent as "the face of data centers."
The Buckeye State, which was namedAmerica's Top State for Business in 2026by CNBC, has become a key battleground for the issue.
OpenAIannouncedin August that it secured 8 gigawatts of computing capacity at the PORTS-Pike Technology Campus in Ohio, thelargestplanned AI data center campus in the world. The first phase of construction is slated to begin this year, and capacity is expected to come online in phases starting in 2028, according to the project'swebsite.
SoftBank and SB Energy are developing the Ohio data center campus in partnership with the U.S. Department of Energy. SoftBank is amajor investorin OpenAI, and the two companies announced plans toinvest $1 billionin SB Energy earlier this year.
Nvidiais backstopping the project, which could cost more than $500 billion in total.
Those plans could now run into resistance from the governor's mansion. Ohio's top office flipped blue on Tuesday, as Democrat Amy Acton, a physician, defeated Republican businessman Vivek Ramaswamy. Acton supports a "conditional moratorium" on data centers to ensure they cover 100% of utility costs and "exclusively build with union labor."
watch nowVIDEO3:1003:10Tech faces a tougher Washington after Democrats flip both House and SenateSquawk on the Street
Heading into the election, the AI trade was already faltering on Wall Street, with chipmakers,neocloudsand other data center-related companies selling off in October on concerns about rising interest rates and overspending. The hyperscalers —Alphabet,Amazon,MicrosoftandMeta— are each spending hundreds of billions of dollars a year on AI infrastructure to meet what they say is insatiable demand. All of those companies except Microsoft have turned cash flow negative in the process.
Getting data center projects off the ground may have just gotten a lot harder.
Communities in California, Florida, Illinois, Kansas, Maine, New Jersey, Nevada and Wisconsin also went to the polls to weigh in on the issue, according to Ballotpedia, and data centers were a key motivating factor for voters in matters up and down the ballot.
In a CNBC Voter Poll, 56% of voters said data centers were a crucial or major factor in their decision, with Democrats ranking the issue higher than Republicans.
Democrats who campaigned on pausing or regulating new projects won key races in Ohio, Wisconsin, Georgia and Texas, which is on track to become the world's largest data center market by 2030.
In one of the most significant results of the night for Democrats, Gina Hinojosa unseated Gov. Greg Abbott after blaming the Republican incumbent for the rapid buildout of data centers across Texas, saying he put the tech industry's interests ahead of local communities.
The losses came despite record spending from Silicon Valley to shape the 2026 midterms, with the GOP boasting a commanding advantage among the election's biggest donors. According to a CNBC analysis of Federal Election Commission records, 14 of the 20 largest donor groups backed Republicans almost exclusively. Crypto, AI and online gambling interests poured in more than $377 million.
Elon Musk, the cycle’s largest individual donor, spent at least $474 million, nearly half of it in Texas, and lost both of the state’s marquee races. It was a warning sign for the wave of tech companies and founders who left California for Texas in search of a friendlier business climate.
"Data centers in space looking pretty appealing right now,"Musk wrotein a post on X.
Elon Musk's record election bet backfired. The backlash may reach beyond one billionaire

AMD's data center revenue nearly doubles and Lisa Su expects growth to accelerate
Google responds to political backlash over removing search from schools that ban AI
Within hours of the polls closing, Democrats were already calling for AI executives to testify under oath.
Among the first to seize on the results was Rep. Greg Casar, the Texas Democrat who chairs the Congressional Progressive Caucus.
"The House Democratic majority must make it a top priority to protect Americans' jobs, freedom, and lives from AI billionaires," Casar said in a statement after Democrats were projected to win the House. "AI company CEOs should be called to testify under oath."
Casar also accused Republicans of being "bought and paid for by AI billionaires," arguing that voters had rejected that influence and warning Democrats to "hold them accountable instead of cashing their checks."
He said the data center fight is only the beginning.
"The revolt against data centers was one of the top issues of the 2026 election," he said. "And in a few years we will look back on it as just the early tremor of a much bigger AI earthquake upending American politics."
Rep. Robert Garcia, D-Calif., the presumptive next chair of the House Oversight Committee, summed it up in two words: "Lawyer up."
— CNBC's Ashley Capoot contributed to this

Midterm ballot measures, from abortion to LGBTQ rights to gunsVoters in dozens of states considered 146 statewide ballot measures this midterm cycle, on topics spanning LGBTQ rights, wealth taxes, abortion, redistricting, guns and more.
Where voters stand on state ballot measures, from abortion to LGBTQ rights to guns
Voters weighed in on 146 statewide ballot measures across dozens of states.Mario Tama/Getty Imageshide caption
toggle captioniMario Tama/Getty Images
Tuesday's midterm elections were a huge sweep for Democrats,among other takeaways.
And across39 states— plus Washington, D.C. and the Northern Mariana Islands — voters weighed in on 146 statewide ballot measures spanning issues from taxes to transgender rights to traffic cameras to data centers and AI.
Here's a look at some of those results.
Three states moved to preserve abortion access
The U.S. Supreme Court overturnedRoe v. Wadein 2022, leaving the legality and regulation of abortion up to each state. In subsequent elections,over a dozen stateshave put access to abortion on their ballots — andoverwhelmingly movedto secure it.
This year, four states considered abortion measures. Three passed, while Idaho voted to preserve the state's abortion ban from 2022.
In Missouri, voters rejected a Republican-led amendment thatwould have banned abortionwith few exceptions. The move affirms support for abortion just two years aftervoters mobilizedto reject Missouri's ban, which was one of the strictest in the country.
Nevada residents voted to enshrine abortion up to the point of viability in their constitution. They did so for thesecond election in a row, since state law requires a proposed constitutional amendment to pass twice.
Virginians voted to create a "fundamental right to reproductive freedom" in their constitution. That includes the right to an abortion during the first two trimesters (and afterward in certain cases), as well as the right to contraception, fertility, postpartum care and more.
Many states considered changes tohow they run their elections.
It was too early to call Wednesday afternoon whether voters had approved some of the more far-reaching changes,in Alaskaand Arizona.
Other states — including Nevada, North Carolina and Ohio — passed measures toughening identification requirements for voters, while California voted against such an effort.
Several states — including Alaska, Arkansas, Kansas, South Dakota and West Virginia — approved measures reinforcing that U.S. citizenship is required to vote in their elections.
Redistricting was also top of mind for voters. President Trump kicked off a redistricting race earlier this year by urging Republican-led states to redraw their districts ahead of the midterms. Republicans and Democrats in multiple states did so. But many of the districts altered to boost GOP prospects ultimately went to Democratic candidates.
Missouri voters rejected aRepublican-friendly congressional map, while Maryland voters passed aredistricting amendmentthat could pave the way for a Democrat-leaning map in 2028.
Virginians passed a measure automaticallyrestoring voting rightsto anyone convicted of a felony once they have completed their sentence.
Virginians also passed a constitutional amendment officiallyrepealing its ban on gay marriageand adding language confirming that the commonwealth will recognize marriage between two adults regardless of their sex, gender or race.
Virginia's ban has been moot since the Supreme Court made same-sex marriage legal nationwide in 2015, but this measure is seen as a safeguard in caseObergefellv. Hodgesgets reversed (assome have fearedin the wake of the court's overturning ofRoe v. Wade). Other states have made similar moves, includingColorado and Californiain 2024.
Vermont overwhelmingly voted to add an amendment to its constitution guaranteeing equal protection under the law "race, ethnicity, sex, religion, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, or national origin."
A number of states considered measures restricting transgender kids' access to school sports teams and gender-affirming care, withColorado passing both.AWashington state measureto ban trans students from competing in girls' school sports was still leading on Wednesday.
Arizonapassed a proposalrequiring schools and athletic associations to restrict students, athletes and employees from using facilities — including restrooms, locker rooms, and other private spaces — that are not designated for their sex assigned at birth. Arizona law already bans trans girls from playing on school sports teams designated for girls, and this measure would extend that prohibition to recreational organizations like Little League.
Taxes and state spending up for debate
One of the most high-profile ballot measures asked Floridians toweigh cutting property taxes for homeowners, which critics say would take billions of dollars in local government revenue away from much-neededpublic serviceslike food banks, libraries, transportation and infrastructure. Voters overwhelmingly passed the amendment.
In California, voters pondered whether to approve a one-off 5%tax on individualswith more than $1 billion in assets, with most of the money raised going toward health care services. The fight against that ballot measure was one of themost expensivein the state's history. The contest istoo close to callas of Wednesday afternoon.
Tennessee voters approved a constitutional amendment prohibiting its government from levying a statewide property tax, which it has not collectedsince 1949. Arizona voters passed a measure that bans cities and towns fromraising taxes on groceriesuntil July 2027. North Carolinians approved an amendment tocap the maximum personal income taxat 3.5%.
Washington voters considered whether to repeal an income tax on individuals and households earning more than $1 million, which is scheduled to take effect in 2028. Earlyresults indicatethey want to keep that tax.
A polar-opposite pair of gun ballot measures
Massachusettsvoted to keepa 2024 law tightening firearm regulations. The law made Massachusetts gun control measures among the strictest in the nation, as it also included requiring "ghost guns" to have a serial number, broadened the definition of "assault-style firearm" and expanded the state's red flag laws.

US voters back abortion rights and reject Trump's gerrymandering in state ballot measures
US voters in several states pushed back on President Donald Trump’s redistricting efforts and backed abortion rights in 145 ballot questions during the midterm elections. Some measures put Trump’s priorities to a public test by gauging support for his attempts to redraw congressional districts, limit reproductive rights and strengthen voter identification requirements.
Issued on:04/11/2026 - 11:49Modified:04/11/2026 - 14:08
6 minReading timeShareBy:FRANCE 24People vote during the US midterm elections at the National WWI Museum and Memorial, in Kansas City, Missouri, on November 3, 2026. © Nathan Howard, Reuters
Abortion-rights advocates notched victories in several states Tuesday, and voters delivered a double dose of disapproval to US PresidentDonald Trump’sredistricting effortsas they decided 145 ballot questions in more than three dozen states.
The ballot measures provided a political undercard for ahigh-profile midterm electionin whichDemocrats took control of Congressandgained power in state legislatures and gubernatorial offices.
Read moreWhy the Democrats routed the Republicans in the US midterm elections
Some measures put Trump’s priorities to a public test by gauging support for hisattempts to redraw congressional districts– a practice also known as gerrymandering – limit transgender athletes in sports andstrengthen voter identification requirements.
Voters defeated a proposed amendment to Missouri’s constitution that would have reimposed restrictions on most abortions. The vote Tuesday essentially reaffirmed voters' decision from two years ago, when they became the first in the nation to undo an existingabortionban by approving an abortion-rights amendment.
The Republican-led Legislature then referred a new, less restrictive version of an abortion ban to this year’s ballot. The measure would have allowed abortions only for medical emergencies and foetal anomalies, or in cases ofrapeorincestup to 12 weeks ofpregnancy. It also would have amended the constitution to prohibit certain medical procedures for transgender minors.
Abortion-rights advocates, led by national progressive groups, heavily outspent abortion foes in a successful campaign to defeat the Missouri ballot measure.
In Virginia, a voter-approved measure creates a "fundamental right to reproductive freedom" in the state constitution, ensuring that abortions can occur during the first two trimesters of pregnancy. The amendment also creates a right tocontraceptionand fertility care, among other things.
An amendment approved in Nevada creates a fundamental right to abortion until fetal viability, which is generally considered after 21 weeks of pregnancy. The amendment won initial voter approval in 2024 but needed a second vote this year to add it to the constitution.
Since the USSupreme Courtoverturned a nationwide right to abortionin 2022, voters in more than one-fifth of the states have passed ballot measures protecting abortion rights.
But voters in Republican-leaning Idaho on Tuesday defeated a ballot measure that would have created abortion rights in state law. Current Idaho law bans abortions unless necessary to save the life of a pregnant woman, or during the first trimester of pregnancy in cases where rape or incest has been reported to law enforcement.
Abortion-rights measures failed two years ago in Florida and South Dakota.
Nine states are using new congressional districts in the midterm elections after a rare spate ofmid-decade redistricting encouraged by Trump.

In Missouri, Republican lawmakers last year adopted new House districts designed to help the GOP win an additional seat in the Kansas City area. Opponents then gathered petition signatures to put the map to a public vote.
The new districts were used in the August primary. But courts subsequently ruled they could not be used again unless first approved by voters in a November referendum. Voters put an end to the new map by rejecting the redistricting legislation on Tuesday.
Meanwhile, voters in Democratic-led Maryland approved a constitutional amendment that could pave the way for new congressional districts in the 2028 election. Democratic proponents, backed by former presidentBarack Obama, had urged a “yes” vote as a way to “stop Trump".
Some Democrats also want to redistrict in Colorado. But a citizen initiative on the ballot would prohibit any potential 2028 redistricting from favouring one political party and require approval from both an independent commission and the state Supreme Court.
An amendment passed Tuesday could wipe away a significant amount of taxes forFloridahomeowners – and leave local governments scrambling for revenue.
The Florida amendment was one of the nation’s most notable property tax proposals in a year when numerous politicians proposed ways to provide tax relief to residents burdened by high costs.
Florida currently exempts the first $50,000 of the value of a person’s permanent residence from many property taxes. That exemption will triple next year for non-school taxes and rise to $250,000 in 2028.
The measure was referred to the ballot during a special legislative session called by Republican Gov.Ron DeSantis. Some local officials warn it could lead to cuts to police and fire departments, public libraries and parks.
Nebraskavoters approved an amendment to add existing transgender medical restrictions to the state constitution. And inArizona, voters passed a measure that extends public school sports restrictions to private schools.
Voters in Colorado and Washington also were considering measuresrestricting transgender athletesor medical procedures. That comes as Trump’s administration has been pushing forrestrictions impacting transgender people, especially youth.

Jesus de Miguel death: Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono 'would never intentionally hurt anyone' says team-mate - BBC Sport
Fans pay respects to Tenerife's De Miguel
ByDavid WatkinsonBBC Sport senior journalist
Goalkeeper Jesus Owono "would never intentionally hurt anyone" and has been "deeply affected" by the death of Tenerife forward Jesus de Miguel, an FC Andorra team-mate said on Wednesday.
Tenerife player De Miguel, 30,died after suffering a serious injury in a collision with Owonoduring a Spanish second division match on Monday.
The world of football has paid tribute to De Miguel, a father-of-one who joined Tenerife in summer 2025, with a minute's silence being held at all European games this week.
Writing on social media, FC Andorra centre-back Lautaro Spatz said Owono was devastated.
He paid tribute to De Miguel but added: "I also want to say a few words about my team-mate, goalkeeper and friend, who is deeply affected by what has happened.
"Those of us who know him know the kind of person he is, how much he is suffering at this moment and that he would never intentionally hurt anyone.
"In football, unfortunate incidents can happen but no-one could imagine that one of them might end with such tragic consequences."
Players from Andorra held a minute's silence before a voluntary training session on Wednesday. Owono did not attend the session.
Football world mourns Tenerife striker De Miguel
Tenerife and Andorra were drawing 2-2 seven minutes into stoppage time when the incident occurred.
Owono ran towards the centre circle to clear a long ball when his knee appeared to collide with De Miguel.
The striker lay motionless on the pitch as medical staff treated him before he was taken by ambulance from Tenerife's Estadio Heliodoro Rodriguez Lopez to hospital.
Owono was sent off and the match was abandoned.
The 25-year-old goalkeeper, who had over 30,000 followers on Instagram on Tuesday morning, has since deactivated his account.
Police in Spain opened a routine investigation into possible involuntary manslaughter following De Miguel's death.
Under Spanish law, any death that is deemed non-natural automatically triggers a judicial inquiry.
Owono has made 47 international appearances for Equatorial Guinea.
The president of Equatorial Guinea's football federation, Venancio Tomas Micha, issued a statement on Tuesday offering "all our human and professional backing" to the player.
"As the involuntary protagonist of this tragic incident in the game, he is living through this situation with deep sorrow and distress," he added.
Jesus de Miguel joined Tenerife in 2025 on a three-year deal
On Tuesday, mourners laid flowers and lit candles beneath a black and white image of De Miguel at the Estadio Heliodoro Rodriguez Lopez.
Tenerife said in a statement they will commence six official days of mourning, with all club activities suspended during this time.
The club's players, staff and officials will attend De Miguel's funeral, which will take place in Navahermosa, Toledo.
Tenerife will also open their home ground on Saturday evening to allow supporters to "bid a fitting farewell".
"Jesus de Miguel's family would like to thank everyone for their messages of support and, from the bottom of their hearts, ask that their privacy be respected at this terrible time. May he rest in peace," added the club statement.
Tenerife and Andorra's Spanish second division matches scheduled for the weekend, against Granada and Mallorca respectively, have been postponed.

The teams have been named, and here they jolly well are!Five changes forLiverpool, with Florian Wirtz and Alexander Isak among those dropping to the bench and Joe Gomez and Kostas Tsimikas among those hopping into the first XI.
Fenerbahce:Ederson, Nelson Semedo, Skriniar, Oppong, Brown, Guendouzi, Kante, Yuksek, Greenwood, Lukaku, Kahveci.Subs:Tarik Cetin, Gunok, Akturkoglu, Demir, Muldur, Muriqi, Mercan, Elmaz, Dorgeles, Aydin, Mimovic.

Earlier today Liverpool’s Under-19sbeat theirFenerbahcecounterparts 5-3, with Will Wright scoring a hat-trick. They were 3-1 up after just 20 minutes, and 4-2 up after half an hour, while Fenerbahce finished with 10 men after Ali Demirbilek was sent off in stoppage time. Also on the scoresheet was Finn Inglethorpe, son of Liverpool’s long-time academy director, Alex.
View image in fullscreenWill Wright of Liverpool scores against Fenerbahce in the Uefa Youth League.Photograph: ANP/Shutterstock
Here’s Andy Hunter’s pre-match missive from Istanbul:
Andoni Iraola has said Liverpool must improve their attacking play but dismissed concerns over the contrast between his team’s output in the Premier League and Champions League.
Liverpool boast a 100% record in Europe this season and can take a significant step towards qualification for the knockout phase with victory away at Fenerbahce on Wednesday.
Iraola’s side failed to register a shot on target, according to Opta, during Sunday’s defeat by Arsenal, the first time Liverpool have drawn a blank in a Premier League home game since their records began in 2003-04. The Liverpool head coach believes the statistic did not reflect his team’s performance but admitted there is room for improvement.
Andoni Iraola calls on Liverpool to sharpen up in attack before Fenerbahce testRead more
Yesterday afternoon former Liverpool striker Dirk Kuyttold the media how excited he was to be facing his former team as Fenerbahce’s interim manager. “As soon as the draw was done, I was really excited because everyone knows how muchFenerbahceand Liverpool mean to me and, from that moment, you know it will be a special occasion,” he beamed. “Of course, tomorrow will be a very special occasion for me but at the stage we’re in, I’m not here for myself. I’m here for the club and that’s what is important, to show the fans who deserve much more, a reaction, positive energy and a good performance.”
Then, at 11.25pm local time last night, the Turkish side announced that former Newcastle midfielder Emre Belozoglu – veteran also of two spells at Fener as a player and one as interim manager in 2021 – was replacing Kuyt, and his special occasion was imperilled. In the cold light of a new day it looks like Emre won’t take over until after this game, at which point Kuyt will either return to the role of assistant he held under previous head coach Ismail Kartal, or leave the club.
Either way, this promises to be a raucous farewell/not farewell. Fenerbahce are having a stinker of a season, sixth in the Super Lig having lost their last two league games, most recently experiencing a Hallowe’en nightmare at home to Goztepe, but this gives them a probably welcome distraction. Let’s see what they do with it, shall we?

NASA Space Grant Students Fuel Agency’s Inspiration Tour
NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman addresses a standing-room-only crowd during an Inspiration Tour stop at Iowa State University.Credit: NASA
NASA’s Inspiration Tour spread the excitement of space exploration and aeronautical innovation by connecting the public, industry, and academia with the people, technologies, and organizations that drive American leadership in space. At nearly every stop across the country,NASA Space Granthas brought students into the heart of the action.
In Iowa, NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman toured the Make to Innovate program lab at Iowa State University. Students from the Iowa Space Grant Consortium’s Mission Moon program, along with consortium-funded student organizations including Cardinal Space Mining, CySat, and CyLaunch, shared research findings and demonstrated the institution’s strong connection to NASA via agency-funded projects. During a well-attended town hall event NASA experts briefed students on the agency’s Moon Base efforts and how their work can contribute to future exploration.
“We’re grateful for the opportunity to welcome NASA leadership to Iowa State,” said Sara Nelson Iowa Space Grant director. “The excitement among students was incredible, and the visit highlighted how the research and innovation happening in Iowa can help advance Artemis and NASA’s future exploration efforts.”
At the University of Arizona, the NASA administrator saw firsthand the space research and engineering capabilities that are enabled by the Arizona Space Grant Consortium. From satellite communications testing to complex optics for peering into deep space to student-built high-altitude balloon payloads and even small satellites, students at the University of Arizona have a long history of contributing to NASA missions and making aerospace career connections. This tour stop also included a Q&A session where the NASA administrator answered questions from local high school and college students.
“It was incredible to present the high-altitude ballooning research we do in SEDS (Students for the Exploration and Development of Space) to Jared Isaacman and those at NASA,” said Ella Miller, a junior studying mechanical engineering at the University of Arizona. “Arizona Space Grant has allowed me to get hands-on experience through an entire mission design process every semester, helping me pursue a career in space research and secure internships in this field.”
Space Grant students from the University of Alaska Fairbanks shared their research with NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman during a Science Fair event in conjunction with the agency’s Inspiration Tour stop.Credit: NASA/Bill Ingalls
At the University of Alaska in Fairbanks, the Administrator toured two Geophysical Institute facilities: Poker Flat Research Range, the university’s scientific rocket launching facility, and the Alaska Satellite Facility. During an Alaska Space Grant science fair, students shared research in hibernation biology and showcased CubeSat technology advancements. Students were also able to learn about the agency’s Moon Base program and ask questions about opportunities available to the next generation of innovators and explorers.
In North Dakota, the Inspiration Tour focused on future exploration capabilities. Space Grant-funded research at the University of North Dakota is helping to shape the future of exploration across STEM fields. Student fellows and NASA interns shared their projects on supercell mergers using satellite imagery, geomagnetic conditions of aurora borealis, and in-situ resource utilization, to name a few. North Dakota Space Grant STEM ambassador students also shared robotics and drone activities as part of “Mission Moon”, which centers Artemis initiatives in statewide collaborations with educators and other North Dakota colleges and universities.
“Getting to speak with the NASA Administrator was an amazing opportunity!” said research fellow and STEM ambassador Malissa Reinhardt. “He genuinely cared about what we students had to say and the research we’re working on, which makes all the hard work we put into our research and North Dakota Space Grant Consortium so rewarding.”
Students at the University of North Dakota’s spacesuit lab demonstrated design advancements for lunar surface spacesuits for NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman during a tour of their lab during the agency’s Inspiration Tour stopCredit: NASA
NASA’s Inspiration Tour will culminate in MAX POWER, a public showcase of air and space innovation on Nov. 7 and 8, highlighting the agency’s commitment to preparing the next generation of innovators and explorers for humanity’s next giant leap. NASA is racing against time to save the Hubble Space Telescope
Date:November 4, 2026Source:NASASummary:NASA is exploring a daring plan to save the legendary Hubble Space Telescope from its eventual fiery plunge into Earth's atmosphere. After more than 35 years of groundbreaking discoveries, Hubble is slowly losing altitude, and without intervention, it could fall back to Earth as early as 2033 or 2034. To keep the iconic observatory operating, NASA is asking private space companies to propose innovative ways to boost Hubble into a higher orbit, upgrade its capabilities, or safely dispose of it when its mission finally ends.Share:FacebookTwitterPinterestLinkedINEmailFULL STORYNASA is exploring a potential rescue mission to save the Hubble Space Telescope from a fiery return to Earth and give it more years to uncover the universe's mysteries. Credit: ESA/Hubble (M. Kornmesser & L. L. Christensen)
NASA is investigating whether private space companies could help extend the life of the Hubble Space Telescope, which has spent more than 35 years transforming our understanding of the universe.
On October 29, the agency issued a Request for Information seeking details about commercial technologies that could be used to service Hubble while it remains in orbit. The goal is to determine whether new spacecraft capabilities could keep the iconic observatory operating longer, improve its performance, or help bring its mission to a safe conclusion.
"Hubble still has important science ahead of it, and we should be looking at every reasonable opportunity to keep it delivering for as long as possible," said NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman. "If there are innovative and cost-effective ways to extend the life of an asset already on orbit, we owe it to the American taxpayer and the scientific community to explore them. Extending Hubble's life would mean more discoveries, more science, and more opportunities to expand our understanding of the universe."
NASA Considers Raising Hubble Into a Higher Orbit
One possibility under consideration is sending a spacecraft to push Hubble into a higher orbit. This could counteract the gradual loss of altitude that threatens the telescope's future and potentially allow it to continue making scientific discoveries for additional years.
NASA is also interested in missions that could service the telescope and improve its capabilities. Another option would focus on safely retiring Hubble when its scientific work is complete, either by guiding it through a controlled descent into Earth's atmosphere or arranging for its disposal in orbit.
These possibilities are being explored rather than formally approved. By reaching out to commercial companies, NASA hopes to better understand what technologies are available and whether they could provide practical, affordable solutions.
"Hubble is a national icon that has fundamentally changed how humanity views our universe for more than 35 years," said Nicky Fox, associate administrator, Science Mission Directorate, NASA Headquarters in Washington. "Commercial industry has rapidly evolved in recent years to offer new capabilities for in-space satellite capture and servicing. Given the time we have until Hubble's anticipated re-entry, we are eager to explore the breadth of possibilities to boost Hubble to a higher orbit while we develop the flagship mission to follow."
Companies interested in participating can reviewNASA's Request for Information online. The agency is accepting responses until 3 p.m. EST on Monday, November 30.
Why Hubble Could Fall Back to Earth by 2034
Although Hubble continues to operate in space, its orbit is gradually shrinking. The telescope travels through low Earth orbit, where traces of Earth's atmosphere create drag that slowly reduces the altitude of orbiting spacecraft.
Even hundreds of miles above the planet, the atmosphere is not completely absent. The tiny amount of remaining gas produces resistance as spacecraft move through it. Over long periods, this effect can cause satellites to lose altitude and eventually descend into denser layers of the atmosphere.
Unlike spacecraft equipped with engines that can periodically raise their orbits, Hubble has no propulsion system capable of maintaining its altitude. Without outside assistance, it cannot reverse this gradual orbital decline.
NASA's current analysis suggests that Hubble will likely reenter Earth's atmosphere sometime between 2033 and 2034. To prevent that outcome through an orbital boost, the agency expects that a mission would need to occur by 2032.
That timeline leaves a limited window to evaluate potential solutions, develop a mission, and carry it out before the telescope descends too far.
Extending Hubble's Legacy of Cosmic Discoveries
Since beginning operations more than three decades ago, Hubble has become one of the most influential scientific observatories ever launched. Its observations have helped reshape astronomers' understanding of the cosmos, and the telescope continues to produce discoveries that advance research across many areas of astronomy.
Hubble is also the product of a longstanding international partnership between NASA and ESA (European Space Agency).
NASA's Goddard Space Flight Center in Greenbelt, Maryland, oversees the telescope and its mission operations, with additional operational support from Denver-based Lockheed Martin Space.
Scientific operations are handled by the Space Telescope Science Institute in Baltimore, which is operated by the Association of Universities for Research in Astronomy on NASA's behalf.
With commercial spaceflight technology advancing, NASA is now evaluating whether Hubble could benefit from capabilities that were not available when it was originally designed. A successful mission to raise its orbit or enhance its systems could allow the historic telescope to continue exploring the universe well beyond its currently projected orbital lifetime.

Israel's president begins consultations with parties after election deadlock - BBC News
President Isaac Herzog received the official results from the Central Election Committee on Wednesday morning
Israel's President Isaac Herzog has begun consultations with political parties on whom to task with forming a new coalition government, after he received the official results of a general election last week he said had no clear winner.
Herzog told party leaders that "not every commitment and promise can be fulfilled" if they want to avoid a new election.
Neither the bloc of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu nor his rival Gadi Eisenkot secured a majority in parliament.
Earlier, electoral officials said there was no evidence of irregularities and that unsubstantiated claims by Netanyahu's camp of Arab-led parties "stealing" the election did not justify delaying the results' certification.
The Shin Bet security service is investigating allegations of foreign interference in the election, but the head of the Central Elections Committee stressed that they would not fundamentally change the outcome.
Israeli opposition accuses Netanyahu of trying to 'delegitimise' election
How could Israel break election deadlock? Here are four scenarios
Israel's election deadlock is a sign of the country's deep divisions
In the election on 27 October, Netanyahu's right-wing Likud party and its far-right and ultra-Orthodox Jewish allies won 53 seats in the 120-seat Knesset. Eisenkot's centrist Yashar party and three other Jewish opposition parties in his bloc won 48.
Two Arab-led alliances, the United Arab List and the Joint List, together won an unprecedented 19 seats following a surge in turnout among Arab voters.
That makes them potential kingmakers. However, all but one of the Jewish parties pledged before the polls not to work with them to form a government.
The role of Israel's president is largely ceremonial, but after an election they have the role of inviting a Knesset member to form a government. That person will be given 28 days to do so, with a potential 14-day extension.
The president has wide discretion to pick someone they believe has the best chance of building a coalition. They do not have to choose the leader of the party with the most seats.
On Wednesday morning, Herzog was presented with the official results by Central Elections Committee chairman Justice Noam Sohlberg at a ceremony in Jerusalem.
"In recent days, we have heard voices trying to cast doubt on the election results and to undermine their legitimacy. This is a real danger," Sohlberg said.
"One of the foundations of democracy is the ability to have a peaceful transfer of power. This stems from the understanding that the will of the electorate obligates us all."
Herzog announced that he would begin the consultation process on Wednesday evening.
"In order to prevent another round of elections and to build a stable and good government here for the people of Israel, I expect the factions and their representatives to understand that, in the current reality, not every commitment and promise can be fulfilled," he said.
The president also expressed confidence in the Shin Bet's ability to investigate the allegations of foreign interference in the election and appealed for patience.
But he warned that Arab Israelis - who make up about one fifth of the population and often refer to themselves as Palestinian citizens of Israel - "must not be smeared".
"I condemn the coarseness and racist expressions that we have heard recently. There is no place for them toward any community in Israel," he said.
Earlier, Sohlberg told a meeting of the Central Elections Committee that the Shin Bet's intelligence appeared to point to a "widespread phenomenon involving the influx of substantial funds into Israel from foreign states", some of which were hostile.
It believed further investigation was needed to "connect the dots and determine the scale of the phenomenon with a high degree of certainty", he said.
Last week, Israeli media reported that the committee had been presented with a claim that Qatar had provided funding aimed at increasing voter turnout in Arab communities. Qatar's foreign ministry said it categorically denied the allegation.
Far-right National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir, the leader of the Jewish Power party and an ally of the prime minister, called on the Shin Bet to arrest all the leaders of Arab parties and interrogate them "until these suspicions are fully clarified".
Joint List chairman Yousef Jabareen accused Ben-Gvir and the prime minister of attempting to "steal the election from the public".
On Tuesday, Eisenkot alleged that Netanyahu and his Likud party were "trying to carry out a veritable pogrom against democracy and the rule of law".
His comments came after Attorney-General Gali Baharav-Miara rejected a reported demand by Shin Bet chief David Zini - an appointee of the prime minister - to interrogate four Arab politicians, saying no evidence of wrongdoing had been presented.
Likud accused Baharav-Miara of trying to "obstruct the investigation and to cover up this serious case of manipulation of the electoral process by foreign actors".

The Israeli president, Isaac Herzog (right), receives official results of the general election from the chair of the Central Elections Committee, Noam Sohlberg.Photograph: Abir Sultan/EPAView image in fullscreenThe Israeli president, Isaac Herzog (right), receives official results of the general election from the chair of the Central Elections Committee, Noam Sohlberg.Photograph: Abir Sultan/EPA
Israel’s election commission rejects Netanyahu claims of voting fraud
Move comes after attorney general blocks Shin Bet call to interrogate politicians from Palestinian-led parties
Israel’s election commission on Wednesday confirmed the final results of last week’s vote that stripped Benjamin Netanyahu’s far-right coalition of its governing majority, rejecting claims of mass fraud promoted by the prime minister.
The main challenger, Gadi Eisenkot, said Netanyahu had launched a “pogrom against democracy” in attempting to hold on to power by discrediting valid votes and weaponising security forces against parties led by Palestinian citizens ofIsrael.
Hours earlier, Israel’s attorney general said she had blocked a demand from the Shin Bet security service to interrogate senior politicians from the Palestinian-led parties because she had not been presented with any evidence of wrongdoing.
“In a country governed by the rule of law, neither citizens nor elected officials can be interrogated without evidence that justifies doing so,” Gali Baharav-Miara said in a statement, after Haaretz reported on the attempt to target four politicians.
Election authorities on Wednesday presented the final results to the president, Isaac Herzog, after rejecting allegations they had been tainted by large-scale foreign interference and voter fraud.
“The review found no evidence of irregularities that compromised the integrity of the election or affected its results,” the Central Elections Committee said in a statement.
View image in fullscreenPeople take part in a rally in Tel Aviv calling for the opposition to form a government with the Palestinian-led parties after last week’s general election.Photograph: Jamal Awad/Reuters
The body’s chair, Noam Sohlberg, said some “suspicions” were still under investigation but “they do not cast doubt on the election as a whole or justify delaying the election results”.
When the results were handed over, Herzog denounced racist attacks on Palestinian citizens who had turned out to vote at historic rates.
“I condemn the coarseness and racist expressions that we have heard recently,” he said. “I hold Arab society in Israel in great respect. I value its contribution to the country in every area of life, and its desire to integrate.”
Herzog will play a key role in the formation of the next government by choosing which politician has the first chance to create a coalition. He is expected to name Eisenkot, and the announcement could come as early as Thursday evening.
A former leader of the Israeli military who lost his son fighting in Gaza, Eisenkot has secured the public support of all of the Jewish Israeli opposition parties. Palestinian-led parties have said their priority is removing Netanyahu, so they are expected to back him as the strongest contender to achieve that.
However, negotiations could take weeks and Eisenkot warned of ongoing attempts to undermine trust in the election results. He accused Netanyahu of weaponising the security services against domestic opponents in an effort to hold on to power.
View image in fullscreenGadi Eisenkot has secured the public support of all the Jewish Israeli opposition parties.Photograph: Paulina Patimer/JNA/Zuma Press/Shutterstock
“The employees of the Ministry of Defense, law enforcement and the civil service in Israel are servants of the state, not the king,” he said in a statement. “Woe to anyone who abuses their authority and role for political considerations.”
The Shin Bet chief, David Zini, handpicked for the role by Netanyahu, had ordered the interrogations and sought to classify the investigation as a security file, which would have allowed harsher conditions including barring the politicians from having legal counsel.
Nadav Eyal, an Israeli journalist and commentator, said the public should brace for more extreme attempts to dismiss election results and discredit the leading opposition parties.
“The groundwork is steadily being laid for violence,” he wrote on X. “What you’re hearing breaking right now is the foundation of the legal and governmental orders in Israel.”
Netanyahu presided over a racist campaign targeting Palestinian citizens of Israel – about 20% of the population – and on election day began promoting the unfounded accusations of mass fraud now rejected by election authorities.
Ahmad Tibi, one of the most prominent and effective Palestinian politicians, was reportedly among those the Shin Bet sought to interrogate. He responded to the latest allegations, as news broke ofsweeping victories for Democratsin the US midterms, with a swipe at Netanyahu’s fear of democracy.
“[The] attorney general is checking suspicion of ties between the Joint List and Democrats in the US,” Tibi wrote in a social media post. “According to the suspicion, in both cases the same sophisticated method was employed: people arrived in droves at the polling stations, cast a slip, and went home.”

He also demanded a freeze on certification and on forming a government. “The elections were stolen, the results are fraudulent, foreign countries interfered,” Ben-Gvir wrote on X, adding that his far-right Otzma Yehudit party would therefore vote against approving the results.
Likud legislator Amit Halevi resigned from the committee. He alleged that some lawmakers “bought their seats with bribe money” and that the vote reflected “the choice of the rulers of Qatar, Iran or Turkey”.Qatar has rejected claimsthat it funded Arab-led parties, calling them “disinformation”.
Haaretz reported that Likud had weighed refusing to recognise the results altogether. Such a move would be unprecedented in Israel and would likely be swiftly overturned by the courts. Sohlberg rejected a Likud demand to discuss the results before certifying them, writing that no party, “however distinguished or senior”, could withhold their publication. He has said even if foreign interference were confirmed, it would not undermine the overall result.
Warning not to erode democracy, Sohlberg said: “There is one thing on which we must agree: election results, as lawfully determined, are binding on us all.”
